statement: If a straight line be cut at random, the square on the whole is equal to the squares on the segments and twice the rectangle contained by the segments.
heath_proof: For let the straight line AB be cut at random at C; I say that the square on AB is equal to the squares on AC, CB and twice the rectangle contained by AC, CB. For let the square ADEB be described on AB, [I. 46] let BD be joined; through C let CF be drawn parallel to either AD or EB, and through G let HK be drawn parallel to either AB or DE. [I. 31] Then, since CF is parallel to AD, and BD has fallen on them, the exterior angle CGB is equal to the interior and opposite angle ADB. [I. 29]  But the angle ADB is equal to the angle ABD, since the side BA is also equal to AD; [I. 5]therefore the angle CGB is also equal to the angle GBC, so that the side BC is also equal to the side CG. [I. 6]  But CB is equal to GK, and CG to KB; [I. 34] therefore GK is also equal to KB; therefore CGKB is equilateral. I say next that it is also right-angled. For, since CG is parallel to BK, the angles KBC, GCB are equal to two right angles. [I. 29]  But the angle KBC is right; therefore the angle BCG is also right, so that the opposite angles CGK, GKB are also right. [I. 34]  Therefore CGKB is right-angled; and it was also proved equilateral; therefore it is a square; and it is described on CB. For the same reason HF is also a square; and it is described on HG, that is AC. [I. 34]  Therefore the squares HF, KC are the squares on AC, CB. Now, since AG is equal to GE, and AG is the rectangle AC, CB, for GC is equal to CB, therefore GE is also equal to the rectangle AC, CB. Therefore AG, GE are equal to twice the rectangle AC, CB. But the squares HF, CK are also the squares on AC, CB; therefore the four areas HF, CK, AG, GE are equal to the squares on AC, CB and twice the rectangle contained by AC, CB. But HF, CK, AG, GE are the whole ADEB, which is the square on AB. Therefore the square on AB is equal to the squares on AC, CB and twice the rectangle contained by AC, CB.
ai_proof_text:
2.4
**Statement:** If a straight line be cut at random, the square on the whole is equal to the squares on the segments and twice the rectangle contained by the segments.

**Step 1.** Let AB be the straight line, cut at random at the point C. I say that the square on AB is equal to the squares on AC and CB together with twice the rectangle contained by AC and CB. On AB describe the square ADEB [1.46], and join DB [P1].

**Step 2.** Since ADEB is a square, it is right-angled [D1.22]; so the straight line AB, falling on AD and BE, makes the interior angles DAB, ABE on the same side equal to two right angles, and therefore AD is parallel to BE [1.28]. In the same way, since the angles ADE, DAB are right, DE is parallel to AB [1.28].

**Step 3.** Through C draw CF parallel to AD, meeting DB at G and DE at F; and through G draw HK parallel to AB, meeting AD at H and BE at K [1.31]. Since CF is parallel to AD and AD to BE, CF is also parallel to BE; and since HK is parallel to AB and AB to DE, HK is also parallel to DE [1.30]. Consequently AHGC, CGKB, HDFG and GFEK are all parallelograms, and ADEB is a parallelogram with diameter DB.

**Step 4.** Since CF is parallel to AD and the straight line DB falls on them, the exterior angle CGB is equal to the interior and opposite angle ADB [1.29].

**Step 5.** Since ADEB is a square, BA is equal to AD [D1.22]; so in the triangle ABD the angle ADB is equal to the angle ABD [1.5]. Therefore the angle CGB is also equal to the angle CBG [CN1].

**Step 6.** In the triangle CGB the angle CGB is equal to the angle CBG; therefore the side CB, which subtends the angle CGB, is equal to the side CG, which subtends the angle CBG [1.6].

**Step 7.** CGKB is a parallelogram (Step 3); therefore its opposite sides are equal, CB to GK and CG to KB [1.34]. But CB is equal to CG (Step 6); therefore the four sides CB, CG, GK, KB are all equal to one another [CN1], and CGKB is equilateral.

**Step 8.** Since CG is parallel to BK and the straight line CB falls on them, the interior angles GCB, CBK on the same side are equal to two right angles [1.29]. But the angle CBK is right, being an angle of the square ADEB [D1.22]; therefore the angle GCB is also right. And the opposite angles of the parallelogram CGKB are equal [1.34], so the angles CGK, GKB are likewise right. Thus CGKB is both equilateral and right-angled, that is, a square [D1.22]; and it is the square described on CB.

**Step 9.** Similarly HDFG is a square. For, HK being parallel to AB and DB falling on them, the exterior angle DGH is equal to the interior and opposite angle DBA [1.29], which is equal to the angle GDH (Step 5) [CN1]; hence HD is equal to HG [1.6]. Since HDFG is a parallelogram, HD is equal to GF and HG to DF [1.34], so that HDFG is equilateral [CN1]. Also the angle HDF is right [D1.22]; DF being parallel to HG and DH falling on them, the angles HDF, DHG are equal to two right angles [1.29], so the angle DHG is right; and the opposite angles of the parallelogram are equal [1.34], so HDFG is right-angled. Hence HDFG is a square [D1.22]. Moreover HG is equal to AC, being opposite sides of the parallelogram AHGC [1.34]; so HDFG is the square on AC.

**Step 10.** Next, AHGC is a parallelogram, and since CF is parallel to AD and AB falls on them, the angles DAC, ACG are equal to two right angles [1.29]; the angle DAC is right [D1.22], so the angle ACG is right, and AHGC is a rectangular parallelogram. Hence AG is the rectangle contained by AC and CG [D2.1]; and CG is equal to CB (Step 6); therefore AG is equal to the rectangle contained by AC and CB.

**Step 11.** In the parallelogram ADEB with diameter DB, HF and CK are the parallelograms about the diameter and AG, GE are their complements; therefore AG is equal to GE [1.43]. Hence GE is also equal to the rectangle contained by AC and CB, and AG together with GE is twice the rectangle contained by AC and CB [CN2].

**Step 12.** Now HF is the square on AC and CK is the square on CB (Steps 8, 9), while AG and GE together are twice the rectangle AC, CB (Step 11). Adding these equals, HF, CK, AG, GE together are equal to the squares on AC and CB together with twice the rectangle contained by AC and CB [CN2]. But HF, CK, AG, GE together make up the whole figure ADEB, which is the square on AB. Therefore the square on AB is equal to the squares on AC, CB and twice the rectangle contained by AC and CB. QED.
